races.name: Cappawhite Civil Engineering 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Balance Of Trade
runners_data.note: Mulligansβ runner has shaped with some promise on Good ground at 10f but the sim-going record (5/12, 0W 0P) over hurdles trips gives no encouragement; a genuine come-from-behind type who will be asked to overcome a compressed hold-up group — the congestion at the rear is the main tactical problem here.
runners_data.comment: Modest Flat record at a lowly level, held comfortably in a claimer at Ballinrobe on his latest outing; handles heavy and yielding ground at around a mile, though inconsistency on the level and the switch to hurdles makes this an obvious ask on debut.

runners_data.name: Boston Benjamin
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's charge has a win on his CV (1/7f Standard) and Kennedy in the saddle is an enormous booking for a maiden hurdle; went 74 days between runs which can sharpen Flat-bred types, and a prominent role suits on this open Limerick track — the most dangerous challenger to the front-runner.
runners_data.comment: From a top jumping operation and successful on the Flat, he makes his hurdles bow wearing a first-time hood; his most recent start at The Curragh was compromised by soft ground and a step up beyond his ideal trip, so stamina over this longer distance remains to be proven.

runners_data.name: Connor Of Mali
runners_data.note: Archdeacon's gelding has been off 266 days — a significant absence flag — and his only hurdles run ended in a tenth-place finish on Good; his natural instinct is to race from off the pace, but with so many hold-up horses in the field he will struggle to find clear daylight late, and the finishing concern tag compounds the worry.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in an auction event at Thurles on his only Flat start, showing little inclination to assert when challenged; returning from a lengthy absence to make his hurdles bow, switching codes on the back of a modest debut makes this a difficult assignment.

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: William Durkan's runner has placed twice at 10f on Standard, hinting at staying ability, but eight and nine-place finishes on Good over this trip suggest the surface isn't bringing out the best in him; drops back into a hold-up pack and will need significant improvement on hurdles debut to feature.
runners_data.comment: Inclined to race too freely, he ran to his mark at Down Royal last time, beaten eight and a half lengths in a maiden on a step up in trip; handles good ground and AW over 7f-10f, though a breathing concern adds a further note of caution on his hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Minella Rockett
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner, and John Nallen's runner has experience over 12f on Standard suggesting he won't be stopping late; the key question is whether Daniel King takes a positive enough hold to dictate a controlling pace — if he does, this horse's jumping rhythm is the most potent weapon in the race.
runners_data.comment: His connections were successful in this contest twelve months ago and he arrives with a respectable level of form from Flat maidens, tiring late on a step up in trip at Dundalk recently; effective at 7f-1m on AW, he is expected to feature on his hurdles debut.

runners_data.name: Nicky Larson
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's 3/14 recent trainer form is worth noting, and O'Keeffe has ridden this horse before; placed second on Good ground at 8f on the Flat and has a cleaner finishing profile than most hold-up rivals here — if any closer can pick through the pack late, this is the one with the most realistic profile for it.
runners_data.comment: Fourth in a handicap at Leopardstown latest, beaten nine lengths on testing ground that may not have suited; he has place form over a mile on soft and yielding going, making him a worthwhile contender on hurdles debut, with stamina the remaining question mark.

runners_data.name: Notahairoutofplace
runners_data.note: Watson's runner has one run to go on — a 14th of 14 over 12f on Good — and carries a "fades in finish" flag that is hard to ignore; Calum Hogan (5) takes the ride, and while the step to hurdles is an unknown quantity, the raw evidence offers very little to work with.
runners_data.comment: Failed to get competitive in an auction race at Fairyhouse on his only outing, well beaten throughout; everything is still to prove over hurdles on debut and it is hard to make a case for him against stronger opponents here.

runners_data.name: Swinging The World
runners_data.note: Denise Foster sends out a horse with a consistent pattern of finishing in the back third (9th, 12th, 12th, 8th, 12th) and the fades-in-finish flag reinforces that; even with a 31-day freshener, it is difficult to construct a scenario where this profile competes for a maiden hurdle prize on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Showed consistency in soft ground maidens at 7f but made no impression in a handicap at Gowran Park on his most recent start; the step up to a hurdle trip on debut raises a genuine stamina question that he needs to answer.

runners_data.name: Words Unspoken
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed — no hurdles form, no sim-going data, running style unknown, and no last-run date recorded; Phillip Enright rides for Susan Curling and this is purely a speculative entry that could either bolt up or trail in, making it the race's single biggest wildcard with no evidence to price it accurately.
runners_data.comment: An 85,000-euro son of Australia making his debut for a yard known to have their newcomers fit first time, and the field is not particularly strong; the dam showed little at 7f as a two-year-old, so pedigree questions exist, though the market could tell the story.

runners_data.name: Sofi's Gift
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's filly carries a 7lb lighter weight (147lbs) than the rest of the field, and with Williamson claiming 5lbs that is a tangible advantage if she stays; all four hurdles runs have ended between 7th and 10th on Good/Soft and the hold-up style means she has a lot of ground to make up from the rear — weight concession is the best argument for her.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths on her handicap debut at Fairyhouse without making any notable impression on the Flat to date; switching to hurdles without meaningful form to build on makes her a difficult choice to support against this opposition.

races.paceDynamic: Minella Rockett is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no immediate challenger likely to contest the early lead, Daniel King can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m½f trip on Good ground at Limerick. The bulk of the field — Balance Of Trade, Connor Of Mali, Divelment, Nicky Larson, and Sofi's Gift — are genuine hold-up types, meaning the race will string out behind Minella Rockett with most runners having to make ground from the middle stages onward. Boston Benjamin is the most credible prominent-running threat and, ridden by Jack Kennedy for Gordon Elliott, is the likeliest horse to actually lock onto Minella Rockett's girth and apply some pressure from second or third. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Balance Of Trade, Nicky Larson, Divelment, and Connor Of Mali are all genuine closers, but with so many sharing that profile, only the sharpest finishers will thread through; Boston Benjamin and Minella Rockett are best placed to dictate, making prominent and front-running profiles the clear tactical beneficiaries in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Minella Rockett Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Minella Rockett is allowed to bowl along at a measured pace unchallenged and the hold-up runners fail to close the gap on the long run-in.
scenarios.body: If Minella Rockett is allowed to bowl along at a measured pace unchallenged and the hold-up runners fail to close the gap on the long run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Kennedy Pegs Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Boston Benjamin travels strongly in second for Jack Kennedy and produces a fluent jump at the last to wear down Minella Rockett on the run-in.
scenarios.body: If Boston Benjamin travels strongly in second for Jack Kennedy and produces a fluent jump at the last to wear down Minella Rockett on the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Splits Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to cause Minella Rockett and Boston Benjamin to tie up inside the final furlong, opening the door for the sharpest hold-up finisher.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just strong enough to cause Minella Rockett and Boston Benjamin to tie up inside the final furlong, opening the door for the sharpest hold-up finisher.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Result — Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart through jumping errors, scrimmaging off the final bend, or an unexpected injection of pace that scrambles the race shape.
scenarios.body: If the race falls apart through jumping errors, scrimmaging off the final bend, or an unexpected injection of pace that scrambles the race shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Boston Benjamin's jumping from the second-last — if Kennedy is travelling on the bridle at that point and Minella Rockett is under pressure, the race will hinge on a clean jump there; any mistake from either leader blows the finish wide open.

Connor Of Mali's 266-day absence makes him a major watch at the first hurdle — a novice jumper returning from nearly nine months off the track is a genuine risk factor for both his own safety and the runners immediately behind him.

With five genuine hold-up types (Balance Of Trade, Nicky Larson, Divelment, Connor Of Mali, Sofi's Gift) all seeking the same ground in the straight, watch for scrimmaging and interference on the run to the last — any runner who gets blocked or squeezed out of a run here will lose ground they cannot recover.

Words Unspoken is completely unexposed and Phillip Enright will not have a pre-formed plan — watch how the horse jumps the first two flights; if it travels fluently and positions naturally off the pace, it becomes a genuine latent danger that the market will have underpriced.

races.name: Cappawhite Civil Engineering Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tuche De Houelle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced French import (only one run in form string), off 412 days — the extreme absence is the dominant concern here; even if talented, a handler with 0 wins from 16 runners in 14 days offers little confidence this comeback is a live one.
runners_data.comment: French dual winner, last successful by one and a half lengths in a hurdle at La Teste De Buch; off a long break for his stable debut wearing first-time tongue-tie, and the layoff combined with the switch of yard mean he needs to acclimatise quickly on these terms.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground profile (3W3P from similar going) and ran a clear career-best last time when winning over a similar trip; Paddy Hanlon (5) is a decent conditional and trainer Hanlon has 2 wins from 26 in 14 days — a genuine player if the hold-up scenario unfolds cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Landed a hurdle at Wexford by three and a quarter lengths two runs ago off a 6lb lower mark; well beaten last time when set too stiff a pace up front, she drops 1lb here and has been effective on sound ground over 2m — there may still be mileage in her mark.

runners_data.name: Youlita
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a recent win to form; C Byrnes is in decent nick (3/15 in 14 days) but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that her chance depends heavily on not being pressured — if the prominent cluster crowds her early she is vulnerable.
runners_data.comment: Back to his best with a narrow chase win at Clonmel last time, despite the jockey dropping the whip late; off a short break now switching back to hurdles, the mark looks lenient given his potential and he handles 2m-2m1/4 on soft or good ground.

runners_data.name: Bop Wont Stop
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a poor recent profile — 0W0P from six similar-going runs and last two efforts both in double-figure finishers; hard to find a compelling angle here and trainer has just 0 wins from 3 in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Inclined to race too freely, he burned himself out when asked to lead up in class at Listowel on his most recent start, finishing well beaten; an inconsistent record in a short career makes him difficult to trust, though the trip and ground with cut do suit.

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy in the saddle is a significant upgrade, and Good ground suits well (9/14 runs on similar ground); ran a placed second on this exact trip in recent form and Elliott's yard is firing with 9 from 65 in 14 days — a leading contender in the prominent scenario.
runners_data.comment: Jumped poorly and made no impression in a handicap at Kilbeggan on his most recent outing; first-time headwear today as connections seek greater consistency, though an erratic recent profile means he needs a significant step up to take a hand here, despite the trip and going suiting.

runners_data.name: Harpy Eagle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who handles Good ground and showed a placed effort at 16f in her history; the 7lb claimer Paddy Cody is notable, and 122 days off the track is a mild stamina-fitness query at this trip, but two decent placed efforts over 19f suggest the distance is fine.
runners_data.comment: Down the field in a handicap at Leopardstown on his most recent start, where the ground may not have suited — he is more effective on a sounder surface over 2m-2m3f; returns from a break wearing first-time cheekpieces, but inconsistency in a short career leaves doubts.

runners_data.name: Silly Mongoose
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 16f on Good and has run five of his last six on Good ground — the going could not be more tailored; trainer has 1 from 6 in 14 days and the hold-up profile fits perfectly in a race where Youlita is expected to control pace.
runners_data.comment: Won a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan by two and a half lengths last time, with traces of inexperience still showing when in front; wearing a first-time hood today and progressing with each run, he is a solid threat over 2 1/2m on good to yielding if that upward curve continues.

runners_data.name: Eastmore
runners_data.note: Extraordinary consistency on Good ground — 14 of his last 15 runs on similar going, with 1W7P from those; Danny Mullins is a top booking, and a Byrnes-trained horse with a track record of place-finding at 16f is exactly the type for the prominent-races-true scenario.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of his last five hurdle starts, second eight lengths off the leader at Tramore most recently when back over a shorter trip; fast ground brings out his best over 2m-2m1/4, and first-time tongue-tie may add a further edge — a consistent performer who is hard to leave out.

runners_data.name: Emesteraye
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a placed third last time on Good (2/4 runs on similar going); Danny Gilligan is a relatively modest claim, and the short form string (four runs) means there is some unknown quantity, but the Going fit is solid.
runners_data.comment: Third on her handicap debut at Wexford most recently, five and a quarter lengths behind the leader in a drop of class; effective over 2m and lightly tried in this sphere, with further progress expected in time, she holds more than an outside chance of getting competitive.

runners_data.name: Regards To Rose
runners_data.note: Won impressively last time out over 16f on Good and handles a range of distances; G B Noonan is a low-profile jockey but trainer McCarthy has 1 from 12 in 14 days — the prominent profile suits this race shape and Good ground is clearly his medium.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Ballinrobe last time, jumping errors not helping on what looked a pipe-opener; she has won over 2m-2m1/2 on good ground and wears first-time tongue-tie today — an inconsistent profile but she has the ability to compete when on song.

runners_data.name: Northern Ruler
runners_data.note: Deeply disappointing recent form (three runs all in 6th or below, including 17th of 17 last time); a genuine hold-up horse whose natural rear position has been redistributed to midfield given the crowded hold-up contingent — the form does not inspire confidence regardless of where he maps.
runners_data.comment: Successful on the Flat but struggling to replicate that form for a new yard over both codes; held comfortably in a maiden hurdle at Naas on his latest start, he returns from a break with first-time tongue-tie and is yet to find his feet over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Inchidaly Copper
runners_data.note: Long absence (242 days) is the primary concern, but his Good-ground form over longer trips is genuinely strong (4W7P from 13 runs on similar going); the field's prominent positions are overcrowded and this horse's natural front-seeking style cannot easily be expressed here — his best chance is a messy or strung-out race.
runners_data.comment: Third seven lengths off the leader at Cork on his most recent hurdle start, running to his mark; the mark looks more workable over hurdles than fences, but this could be a stiff enough examination on his return and he has more to prove at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Youlita is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead identified, she is expected to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m½f at Limerick. Dairy Force, Harpy Eagle, Regards To Rose, and Eastmore all carry prominent profiles and will press forward behind her, creating a bunched early order rather than a strung-out procession. Inchidaly Copper is a natural prominent type who has been redistributed to midfield because there are more pace-seeking horses than can realistically hold those positions — Youlita, Dairy Force, and Eastmore are the likeliest to actually secure the front rank given class and jockey firepower. With Youlita likely to control a genuine but not blistering tempo, and the prominent cluster tight behind, this race shape most favours hold-up horses who travel smoothly in mid-rear and have the finishing kick to pick off a slightly flattering pace — horses like Silly Mongoose, Mo Ghille Mar, and Emesteraye are best placed to exploit that scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Youlita Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Youlita sets a sustainable front-running tempo that flatters prominent types before the home straight.
scenarios.body: If Youlita sets a sustainable front-running tempo that flatters prominent types before the home straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster behind Youlita results in a genuinely contested gallop that suits those who race close to the pace throughout.
scenarios.body: If the prominent cluster behind Youlita results in a genuinely contested gallop that suits those who race close to the pace throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies
scenarios.trigger: If Youlita's controlled lead becomes truly uncontested and the field fails to mount a coordinated challenge from behind.
scenarios.body: If Youlita's controlled lead becomes truly uncontested and the field fails to mount a coordinated challenge from behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lottery — Late Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, a messy pace, or traffic trouble at hurdles causes the race to break down into an unstructured scramble.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors, a messy pace, or traffic trouble at hurdles causes the race to break down into an unstructured scramble.

watchPoints.text: Youlita's control of the gallop is the race's fulcrum — if Dairy Force or Regards To Rose press her hard after the second flight, the tempo will rise sharply and the hold-up horses' task becomes dramatically easier.

Inchidaly Copper returns from 242 days off and cannot realistically find his natural prominent position in this field — watch for early positioning problems that could see him get detached or forced very wide.

Tuche De Houelle has not raced in 412 days and has a trainer with 0 wins from 16 recent runners — any market confidence should be treated with caution as a potential course-money move rather than genuine form evidence.

Eastmore is trained by C Byrnes alongside Youlita — if Eastmore sets a target from prominent, Youlita's jockey may ease slightly, effectively engineering a stable-favoured tempo; watch how both horses travel in the first mile.

The Good ground is uniform across all eight races on the card — no specific ground bias towards one part of the track has been flagged, but Silly Mongoose and Eastmore both carry the strongest same-going profiles in the field and warrant monitoring as the race develops.

races.name: Kevin McManus Bookmaker Grimes Hurdle (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Jesse Evans
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old with a superb record on Good ground (15 runs, 4 wins, 11 places) and a fine recent second at this track over similar distance, he races prominently and gives trainer Noel Meade a live each-way angle; 31 days since last run is straightforward and Sam Ewing takes the ride on a horse who handles this trip and going combination extremely well.
runners_data.comment: Landed a chase at Listowel by nine lengths last time, thriving under a positive ride at a shorter trip; successful in this race twelve months ago and a proven operator in Graded company over 2-2 1/2m, he wears first-time tongue-tie and poses a genuine threat if this becomes a thorough examination.

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old returns after 87 days but showed smart form when winning on Good ground earlier in his career, and Jack Kennedy's presence is a significant booking that suggests the yard is confident; he'll want to race prominently and his last two hurdle wins came on Good to Yielding, making the ground here entirely manageable.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a Grade 2 at Fairyhouse when the race didn't unfold to suit his style; hugely progressive prior to that setback and now back in handicap company with a first-time hood and a top jockey aboard — he remains a real threat over 2-2 1/4m on any ground.

runners_data.name: Daddy Long Legs
runners_data.note: Paul Townend rides the confirmed front-runner for Mullins, and this horse has shown a clear preference for making the pace — his one win on Good ground came from the front — but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) is a reminder this is not his natural hurdles shape and he has an uneven recent record including a fifth at a short trip; he dictates here but his effectiveness against better-class rivals is the question.
runners_data.comment: His connections have landed four of the past ten runnings here, and he returns to hurdles on a sound surface that suits after a recent run on the Flat; consistent at the top level and wearing first-time cheekpieces today, he carries the best form credentials and looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: King Of Kingsfield
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up horse from the Elliott yard, he has a solid record on Good ground at this class, winning at Gowran over 18f on Good and placing at Limerick, and Josh Williamson is an emerging young jockey; needs the race to develop into a stamina test to deploy his hold-up style to best effect, and a recent run of disappointing efforts (31P66) demands scrutiny.
runners_data.comment: Burned himself out when pressed hard in front in a Grade 1 chase last time and was well held; returns from a break with first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and while 2m is his best trip, this grade may have found him out and he could fill a pacemaking role.

runners_data.name: Run For Oscar
runners_data.note: The most significant flag here is 259 days off the track — a very long layoff for a nine-year-old hold-up horse — and while his form when fresh has been competitive on Good ground, Danny Mullins cannot paper over that much of an absence without a race under his belt; his best form over 22f suggests he may find this 2m½f trip on the short side at his preferred end of the stamina spectrum.
runners_data.comment: Lost his rider at a hurdle on his final start before a lengthy absence; a thorough staying type who gets 3m over hurdles and was in good form when last completing — first-time cheekpieces added today, though getting back to his best after such a long layoff is the key question.

runners_data.name: Barbizon
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old won twice at Haydock on Good and has course form, but this is his most competitive assignment and he arrives after 114 days off — a natural prominent racer whose chance is further compressed by being mapped away from his favoured position in a field with several similar types ahead of him; the STYLE_FIT (0.93) flag tempers expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in a juvenile handicap hurdle most recently, finding the company too strong; progressive on the Flat and a useful recruit in theory for a leading yard, but he needs easier conditions to show that potential — back from a break with first-time tongue-tie and out of his depth here.

runners_data.name: Queenofthelodge
runners_data.note: Shane Curling's six-year-old mare won over 20f on Good ground and comes here off a 37-day break in reasonable nick, but she runs at the bottom of the weights against higher-rated rivals and — though she naturally wants to race up with the pace — there is no room to do so comfortably in this configuration; the redistribution to midfield is a genuine tactical handicap for her chances.
runners_data.comment: Fourth beaten 17 lengths at Ballinrobe on her latest outing, not at her best back in a handicap; generally on an upward curve and wears first-time cheekpieces today, but the current mark looks to be at the limit of her ability and she must bounce back sharply from that display.

races.paceDynamic: Daddy Long Legs is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival willing to challenge from the front, Paul Townend can dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the outset on Good ground at Limerick over 2m½f. Jesse Evans and Bowensonfire will press into prominent positions just off the pace, meaning the early order is orderly rather than contested, and the tempo is likely to be honest but never frenetic. King Of Kingsfield and Run For Oscar will settle into hold-up positions from which they need the race to truly test stamina in the closing stages. The field does carry more genuine prominent-running types than can all slot into their natural berths — Barbizon and Queenofthelodge are both natural front-to-prominent racers who are pushed into midfield on this map, meaning their true role is compressed and their effectiveness is reduced. This race shape — a single front-runner controlling an even gallop with prominent types close behind — strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final obstacles, rewarding tactical efficiency over late finishing speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Daddy Long Legs Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Daddy Long Legs bowls along at a sustainable clip and none of the prominent types apply serious pressure.
scenarios.body: If Daddy Long Legs bowls along at a sustainable clip and none of the prominent types apply serious pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold On Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is just quick enough to blunt the front-runner and one of the close-tracking prominent types picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is just quick enough to blunt the front-runner and one of the close-tracking prominent types picks up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens sufficiently mid-race to string the field out and create a stamina test that rewards late-closers.
scenarios.body: If the gallop quickens sufficiently mid-race to string the field out and create a stamina test that rewards late-closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the race dissolves into chaos — a fall, a jumping blunder, or a dramatic collapse in the front rank — and a lower-rated runner profits.
scenarios.body: If the race dissolves into chaos — a fall, a jumping blunder, or a dramatic collapse in the front rank — and a lower-rated runner profits.

watchPoints.text: Watch Barbizon and Queenofthelodge at the start — both are natural prominent types jostling for a position that is already spoken for, and any scramble or interference in the early stages could unsettle the entire field behind Daddy Long Legs.

Monitor Daddy Long Legs's jumping closely — Paul Townend sets the tempo but this horse has form over shorter trips and fences, and any hesitation or error at a hurdle at the head of affairs on Good ground could bring the race to a head earlier than expected.

Run For Oscar's 259-day absence is a serious flag in Grade 3 company — watch his market move and in-running demeanour through the early stages, as a rusty jumper returning from this long a break at 2m½f could easily get outpaced before his stamina tells.

King Of Kingsfield needs to peel wide and make ground from off the pace; watch how Josh Williamson positions him turning for home — if he is trapped behind the prominent pack with no daylight, his hold-up chance is effectively neutralised in a race unlikely to fall apart late.

runners_data.name: Boomerang Breeze
runners_data.comment: Alkaadhem gelding from a pedigree that offers some encouragement — dam showed ability from a mile to 14f and a half-sibling has proved useful over longer trips. The stable rarely makes an impact with newcomers, however, so he is best treated as a watching brief on debut.

runners_data.name: Calzaghi
runners_data.comment: Flat-bred gelding effective over 10-12f on the level but jumping errors proved his undoing at Listowel most recently, where he finished well adrift while showing signs of immaturity; more likely to find his niche in a handicap context in time than make a big impact in a race of this nature.

runners_data.name: Capri Gear
runners_data.comment: Never in contention on debut at Ballinrobe, well beaten throughout and failing to land a blow; a clear second string for the yard here and seemingly in need of more time and experience before he can be expected to compete meaningfully in maiden hurdle company.

runners_data.name: Denham Rock
runners_data.comment: Beaten some way off the pace in his three starts to date, though he made small forward strides at this course most recently; the step up in trip on offer today is a positive angle on paper, but he needs to find considerably more to trouble the better-fancied runners.

runners_data.name: Freddie's Back
runners_data.comment: Point winner who has produced strong hurdles form at this track, finishing third in a race where a stronger gallop would have suited him better; effective at 2m5f on soft and likely to progress over longer trips as his career develops, adding first-time tongue-tie on return from a break.

runners_data.name: Goodmancon
runners_data.comment: Experienced in bumpers and has shown enough promise over hurdles to rate as a genuine contender; beaten 6l at Tramore most recently in a fair effort and effective at this trip on both good and yielding going, with inconsistency in his recent record the main caveat.

runners_data.name: Jack Owen Jack
runners_data.comment: Highly promising on hurdles debut at Listowel, reaching the frame 4l third despite jumping poorly throughout; handles this trip on good ground and first-time tongue-tie should help sharpen his technique having learnt a great deal from that initial run — the clear one to beat on merit.

runners_data.name: Lord Lackendarra
runners_data.comment: Well held at Killarney most recently despite being given every opportunity, though inconsistency has been a feature of his bumper campaign; back after a short break and adaptable to any going at 2m, suggesting the move to hurdles could help him find a more reliable gear.

runners_data.name: No Mon No Fun
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete at Ballindenisk most recently and showed little in his point-to-point career, so there is plenty to prove before he can be trusted; first-time tongue-tie is a sign connections are seeking a remedy, but he remains very much a work in progress at this stage.

runners_data.name: Riverstown Boy
runners_data.comment: Showed some potential at Clonmel on his hurdles debut, fading only in the closing stages as though a longer test would suit; today's step up in distance is a clear positive angle, though two pulled-up starts in his recent record leave some doubt about his jumping under pressure.

runners_data.name: Rusty Finure
runners_data.comment: Poor form in bumpers has been persistent, most recently finishing well beaten at Listowel, and nothing so far suggests a prompt change of gear now hurdling; a sizeable improvement in his performances is a prerequisite for any involvement here.

runners_data.name: Siege Of Carthage
runners_data.comment: Well held at Wexford most recently when faster ground and the extra distance failed to suit, but a placed bumper effort shows he is not without ability; effective at 2m2f on heavy and the move to hurdles looks a sensible direction, with more expected from him in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Venture Maximus
runners_data.comment: Debut Mahler gelding out of a dam that placed over hurdles, though his half-sibling failed to make much of an impression over extreme distances; no obvious edge in the market and best treated as a watching brief until he has shown something in a first run.

runners_data.name: Open Approach
runners_data.comment: A big player at Downpatrick on his second start, travelling with purpose and beaten only 4l in a manner suggesting the longer the trip the better; handles good ground and our figures rate him second here — more scope in the locker and a genuine threat, with today's distance possibly stretching just short of his ideal.

runners_data.name: Becca Sommers
runners_data.comment: Made her debut at this course and, while a 35l fourth, she at least stayed on to complete the 2.5m trip; she may improve a fraction from that initial experience, but faces a stiff ask to get competitive from this position on such limited evidence.

runners_data.name: Latopix
runners_data.comment: Landed a French bumper and has been building on that foundation with her current yard, finishing 3l second at Punchestown most recently when stepped up in distance — her most encouraging outing under rules; effective on good and cut ground over a range of trips and a genuine danger, with a slight drop in distance the only uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Secret Moon
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on her sole start in a maiden point at Dawstown and showed little of note throughout; the switch to hurdles after a short break offers a clean slate, but there is scant evidence she can make an impression on rivals of this quality.

runners_data.name: Torque De Lune
runners_data.comment: Beaten 11l at Downpatrick latest in a run where a stronger test appeared to be the answer, and she usually settles in the rear waiting for the gallop to quicken; effective at 2m2f and may improve for a longer trip, though a mixed jumping record adds to the risk.

runners_data.name: Gc Star Speed
runners_data.comment: Debut mare by Lucky Speed with pedigree interest — a half-sister showed ability over longer distances and another half-sibling has gone well over points and hurdles; on known evidence, though, she is best observed rather than backed until she has demonstrated something on a first public start.

runners_data.name: Matcho d'Agrostis
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way at Punchestown most recently having made no impact throughout, and while his debut form carries some credentials at a high level, a big jump in performance is needed; looks better suited to lower-grade handicap company in time and hard to be confident about in this field.

runners_data.name: Mambo Du Large
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on his hurdles debut at Clonmel while making repeated jumping errors throughout; likely to need considerably more time before realising any potential over hurdles and remains a significant risk in this company at the present stage of his career.

races.name: Joe Walsh Flooring Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bhean Saibhre
runners_data.note: Consistent in similar going — three placing efforts on Good or Soft — and Peter Smithers' 7lb claim gives a real weight advantage; her natural prominent style should allow her to slot in directly behind Cocovic and she is one of the truest pace-map fits in this race.
runners_data.comment: Landed a maiden hurdle earlier in the season but the form may have flattered her, and she was found wanting at Ballinrobe on her most recent start; effective at up to 2m2f on good and heavy ground and runs in first-time tongue-tie, though recent evidence raises doubts about her current level.

runners_data.name: Cocovic
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner stepping into a prominent role here, flagged STYLE_FIT 0.93 — has placed twice over this trip on Good but is essentially asked to race below his natural lead position; his chance depends on whether he can dictate comfortably or is swept past approaching the straight.
runners_data.comment: Back to form at this course last time, doing best of those held up to finish third after a break in running; handles good and yielding at today's trip and expected to strip fitter for that outing — first-time hood on and rated here as a lively candidate from what looks a fair mark.

runners_data.name: Desert Cave
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes takes over on an 8yo who has been struggling for form (0-6565 latest), and his hold-up style on Good ground over 2m+ has not produced a win in 15 similar-going starts; the trip and surface are fine but current form is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Form has been poor since his return from a lay-off, most recently well beaten at Kilbeggan, and there is little to suggest an immediate revival; first-time cheekpieces bring an element of the unknown and he handles this trip on a sound surface, but hard to recommend in his current state.

runners_data.name: Global Skies
runners_data.note: Won his last two starts over 2m on Good ground which is a strong recent profile, and Danny Gilligan has been in form; races from hold-up position and will need a gap to open from off the pace, but the form clock is ticking positively.
runners_data.comment: Flat-bred horse who has been progressing in hurdle handicaps, landing his most recent start by 5l at Clonmel off a mark 9lb lower on better ground; effective at today's distance on good to yielding and runs in first-time hood, with the rise back up the weights now the examination he faces.

runners_data.name: Qaasid
runners_data.note: Won on Soft 25 days ago and has placed at this kind of trip before; Paddy Hanlon's 5lb claim helps in a 15-runner handicap, though his prominent style means he must actively compete for position and his Good-ground record shows 0 wins from 11 similar starts — form conversion is the question.
runners_data.comment: Won a hurdle earlier this season and was in good order before his most recent outing at Punchestown, which perhaps arrived a race too soon — he finished down the field; effective at this trip with cut in the ground and on what looks a fair mark, with first-time cheekpieces applied as connections seek to recapture his earlier form.

runners_data.name: The First Turn
runners_data.note: Has won twice over 2m on Good ground and goes well at Limerick-style right-handed tracks; hold-up style suits this race shape less than Scenario B, but a 5yo with a rising profile who is 1W1P from five similar-going runs and handles the trip.
runners_data.comment: Connections have a strong record in this contest, and The First Turn looks a likely type to step forward in handicap company; usually held up and fourth at Punchestown latest having shown he handles this trip on good ground, with the pulled-up effort on his previous start the main question mark.

runners_data.name: General Clermont
runners_data.note: A 10yo veteran who has finished 2nd twice and placed six times in 14 Good-ground starts without a win in this going — honest and reliable but pattern suggests he fills places rather than takes them; prominent style should see him in touch throughout.
runners_data.comment: Last seen failing to complete at Kilbeggan in a race that appeared to come too soon after a previous engagement, but his chasing form suggests he could be well treated on his hurdle mark; effective over a wide range of trips on any going and simply needs to bounce back to his better level to be a major factor.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: 269 days off the track is a significant flag for a 5yo, and the amateur rider Finn Tegetmeier is an unknown quantity here; was placed in all five recent Good-ground runs including a win over 2m4f, so the form profile is interesting if fitness holds — watch closely in market.
runners_data.comment: Fine form over both hurdles and fences prior to his lengthy absence, and second at Tipperary on his final run before the break, fading only in the closing stages over a longer trip; his hurdle mark looks lenient given his capabilities, but returning after 269 days off the course is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Warm In Gorey
runners_data.note: Two placings from his last two runs 19 days ago suggest he is in a purple patch; blinkers applied, prominent style suits tracking a single pace-setter, and Good ground is fine — but has not won in 15 similar-going runs (0W7P), making him a habitual placer.
runners_data.comment: Third at Downpatrick most recently, matching his established level in a consistent effort at this trip — he handles the distance and is generally reliable over hurdles; first-time blinkers are a new element and he has every right to be a serious rival here, with the three pulled-up runs in his more distant form the only doubt.

runners_data.name: The Vegas Raider
runners_data.note: Back after 437 days off the track, which is a major concern regardless of ability; a genuine prominent type who is mapped to midfield here because the prominent positions are full, and the long layoff combined with racing out of role makes this very difficult to assess positively.
runners_data.comment: Back after an absence of over a year, wearing first-time tongue-tie and visor; his best efforts came on a decent surface and his mark gives him a chance on paper if the ability has been preserved, but the lengthy layoff means everything must be proved anew before he can be backed with confidence.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Paradise
runners_data.note: A 5yo with Alan O'Sullivan (5lb claim) who landed a win seven runs ago but has not placed in four starts since; hold-up style and Good ground are fine, but the form has dipped and the trainer has only one runner in the last 16 days.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Wexford on her most recent start after returning from a break, performing to her level but fading a little in the closing stages over today's trip; effective at 2.5m and could make more of an impact now she steps into handicap company, though she needs to find an extra gear to threaten the principals.

runners_data.name: Pure Logic
runners_data.note: A true prominent racer who is shown in midfield because the prominent berths are taken — his natural rhythm will be disrupted, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 combined with 0 wins from 8 similar Good-ground starts makes this a tough afternoon for him.
runners_data.comment: Held her form at Downpatrick last time, beaten 4l but lacking the extra pace when the race quickened; effective at around 2m on good ground and adds first-time cheekpieces, though the trainer's current tally of 0 from 29 in the past fortnight is a notable concern and she remains yet to score.

runners_data.name: Committee Meeting
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who is mapped to midfield due to redistribution — his recent form reads U/80-P which is poor, and blinkers have not sparked improvement; the style displacement compounds an already weak form profile.
runners_data.comment: A pattern of declining form since returning from a lay-off, most recently failing to complete at this venue; effective over the trip and first-time blinkers represent a change of approach, but he has been going in the wrong direction and needs a significant improvement in form to get involved.

runners_data.name: Friar Hogan
runners_data.note: Has a noted tendency to fade in the finish, and is redistributed from his natural hold-up position into a midfield mapping — that combination of flagged fitness concern and style disruption significantly undermines his prospects; form of 060-0C (completed unknown) on soft going mainly is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Denied a chance to complete at this venue most recently after being carried out on ground that was on the soft side, though his earlier record offers little encouragement either; first-time tongue-tie represents a change of tack, but until he shows something more convincing he remains hard to support here.

runners_data.name: Cullenwaine
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 2m6-7f on Good ground with three seconds in recent starts; a natural prominent type bumped to midfield, but Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim and a low OR of 80 mean he carries far less than market rivals — if he can recover position early, do not ignore him.
runners_data.comment: On a lengthy losing run but has shown renewed form over fences, and twice placed in recent starts; held at Tramore last time when perhaps ridden too prominently, and first-time blinkers may help him settle — effective at this trip and arguably lenient on earlier figures, though he remains yet to score.

races.paceDynamic: Cocovic is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with the field at 15, is likely to get a relatively uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m4f — a setup that rewards those racing prominently or tracking close to the pace rather than those coming from deep. The prominent berths, however, are oversubscribed: Bhean Saibhre, Qaasid, General Clermont, Mickey Cohen, and Warm In Gorey all want to race near the pace, meaning several will be squeezed out of their natural position before a hurdle is jumped. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure those positions — Bhean Saibhre and Qaasid look most likely to actually land prominent berths, while The Vegas Raider, Pure Logic, and Cullenwaine are genuine prominent horses who will be shuffled back into midfield against their wishes. With a single, unhurried pace-setter and a congested midfield, this race shape most directly favours confirmed prominent racers who can travel close to Cocovic's honest but unforced fractions, and those hold-up types who find cover and save enough energy to deliver a clean, sustained finish on the Good surface.

scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group quickens entering the straight and burns off each other, opening a lane for hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: If the congested prominent group quickens entering the straight and burns off each other, opening a lane for hold-up horses to sweep through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Two Clear

scenarios.body: If the pack sets too competitive a tempo in the early stages fighting for prominent positions, leaving Cocovic and the one horse tracking it to dominate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scramble, Outsider Lands

scenarios.body: If redistributed prominent types like Cullenwaine or The Vegas Raider find themselves racing at their natural pace from further back and the race becomes messy throughout.

watchPoints.text: Bhean Saibhre and Qaasid are both natural prominent horses competing for the same space behind Cocovic — one of them will be squeezed out early and forced to race against their style, which could produce a troubled run or a dramatic switch in tactics.

Mickey Cohen returns after 269 days off the track with an amateur rider — watch the market closely pre-race; if gambled on, the stable may have him primed, but blind faith on seasonal debut in a 15-runner handicap carries real risk.

Cullenwaine carries only 140lbs (OR 80) which is 20-plus pounds less than the top weights — Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claim adds to that, and in a race where several prominent types race out of position, he may sneak into contention from a low weight if he recovers his natural berth.

The Vegas Raider (437 days off) and Committee Meeting (U/80-P recent form, redistributed) are two runners whose race-day behaviour in the parade ring and at the start may reveal their readiness — both are difficult to recommend on paper but worth monitoring if they move well pre-race.

races.name: Munster Suite At Limerick Races Handicap Hurdle (0-100) (Div 1)

runners_data.name: Charlie's Dilemma
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; has won over 19f on Good and gets an ideal solo lead but its STYLE_FIT flag hints it may be racing beyond its ideal comfort zone — watch how it jumps early.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, he has struggled since returning from a layoff, being well beaten when outpaced at Ballinrobe last time. Blinkers fitted today as connections try a new angle; effective over today's trip and going, but needs to find considerably more.

runners_data.name: Illtakehimmyself
runners_data.note: Consistent recent form with back-to-back runner-up finishes, travels prominently and handles Good ground well over this sort of trip; five-pound claimer Calum Hogan can help manage the weight.|
runners_data.comment: A pair of runner-up efforts in his last two outings mark him out as a genuine threat, and he handles today's going well; progressive profile and with more to offer, particularly over a more demanding stamina test. First-time tongue-tie applied; still to get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Any Chance
runners_data.note: Running style is genuinely unknown from the data supplied, making it difficult to assess where it will settle in the pack; Good ground suits on limited evidence but no wins from sim-going runs.|
runners_data.comment: Held on his handicap debut at Wexford, though the going could have been on the quick side that day; handles today's softer conditions better and looks the type to progress further now settling into handicap company. Yet to win, but retains scope for improvement on these terms.

runners_data.name: Stretchemout
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who won over 21f on Good ground and comes back from 232 days off — strip fitness is the key question, but the tongue-tie and trip tick boxes if fit.|
runners_data.comment: Off the track for 232 days, she returns to hurdling in a first-time tongue-tie after pulling up in a chase where the ground proved too soft. Has shown ability at today's distance and conditions at her best, but has plenty to prove after such a lengthy absence.

runners_data.name: Sallap
runners_data.note: Two wins in recent form but the fade-in-finish flag is a concern over this extended 2m6½f trip; hold-up style means it needs a true gallop to peg back the front-runners.|
runners_data.comment: Top-rated in the field, she landed a handicap hurdle at Clonmel last time, drawing away by over three lengths off a lower mark and travelling strongly throughout; typically held up and appears to be developing well as she gains more experience over staying trips. Effective over today's trip and going, and the one to beat.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose best recent run was a close third over 22f on Good; her jumps record includes falls so jumping fluency will matter in a big field.|
runners_data.comment: Returned to hurdling with a down-the-field effort here most recently, and her record across points and hurdles has been patchy; showed some promise when runner-up in her last few outings, and she handles today's trip and going. Hard to rely on, though not without claims if producing her best.

runners_data.name: Le Fanu
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 20f on Good and races prominently — that combination suits this shape well; the age (10) is a query but trainer Walsh has him in form right now.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Listowel last time, going up in trip to score by over two lengths off a lower mark; consistent profile and may have more in reserve now he has opened his account. Effective on today's going, though the further step up to 22 furlongs may test his stamina.

runners_data.name: Ocean Murphy
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old hold-up type with limited sim-going evidence; long absence of 95 days is a concern, and the heavy-bias in past form suggests Good may not be its best surface.|
runners_data.comment: Held up as usual, he was well beaten at Downpatrick on his latest start, left with too much ground to cover over a shorter trip; first-time cheekpieces today as he returns from a short break. Handles today's distance with cut in the ground, though his trainer is currently going through a lean spell.

runners_data.name: Stumblin In
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good ground but struggles to win — 13 runs on sim-going with only one win; a tongue-tie runner who tends to sit off the pace and rarely quickens decisively.|
runners_data.comment: Held in recent outings over shorter trips, she appeared to need a more searching test at Clonmel last time; stepping back up in distance today in a first-time tongue-tie, and she handles today's going and trip. Yet to score in her last five starts, but the return to further looks a positive.

runners_data.name: Friends Of Barry
runners_data.note: Finished second over 22f on Good last time and carries the fade-in-finish warning; a hold-up profile means it relies on the pace being strong enough to bring it into contention.|
runners_data.comment: Stepped up in trip and dropped in class at Tramore last time, finishing second off a lower mark; an encouraging run, and he handles today's distance and going. In cheekpieces today; yet to score in recent starts, but the form is heading in the right direction.

runners_data.name: Whatafoolbelieves
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping due to overcrowding at the rear; fade-in-finish flag combined with out-of-role positioning make a winning run from this shape very unlikely — the McConnell yard has been quiet.|
runners_data.comment: Well held in his last five outings, including well beaten at Sligo most recently; yet to demonstrate anything at this level and struggling throughout. First-time cheekpieces fitted today, but with his trainer going through a difficult run of results, he holds little appeal here.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with experience over this trip, decent recent form and J J Slevin in the saddle is a major plus; the tongue-tie and pads suggest the stable wants a forward-going display today.|
runners_data.comment: Rates highly on our figures despite a patchy recent record; failed to respond to blinkers when pulled up in a handicap chase at Downpatrick last time. Returns to hurdling today in first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and may benefit from stepping slightly beyond two and a half miles in time. Capable of better on his day, but inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Ballinaboola Gold
runners_data.note: A naturally rear-dwelling type forced into midfield mapping; showed improvement with a second over 24f on Good recently, and Danny Mullins adds class, but racing out of role limits the upside.|
runners_data.comment: Her second-place finish on her penultimate start showed what she can do on her day, though she ran well below that level at Wexford last time and can be unreliable. Handles today's going and is effective at this trip; yet to score but a threat if she reproduces her better form.

runners_data.name: Can't Catch Molly
runners_data.note: Poor recent form string with consecutive zeros; a true hold-up horse placed in midfield due to field redistribution, which only compounds the challenge — no wins from five sim-going runs.|
runners_data.comment: Briefly threatened at this course last time before fading when stepped up in trip; returning from a short break and may still need time to fully develop. Acts on heavy ground, but winless in her last five starts and faces strong opposition in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Liss Eile
runners_data.note: Has shown a hint of form over 16f on Good (4th last time) but is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into midfield representation; the shorter trip history and out-of-role mapping both work against it here.|
runners_data.comment: Down the field at Clonmel most recently, though that outing perhaps arrived before she was ready; still to translate that earlier promise into results and remains winless in recent starts. First-time cheekpieces today; best at 2m on today's going, but hard to trust at this level.

runners_data.name: Stone Rulya
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old with a consistent back-of-the-field profile and a fade-in-finish flag; held up in a naturally held-up field means it has been remapped to midfield — the step up in trip is notable but form figures give little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: Green and never travelling at Clonmel most recently, with no wins in his last four starts; has not shown enough over obstacles in terms of stamina or jumping, and needs significant improvement. Blinkers fitted today, but hard to see him troubling more experienced rivals from this form.

runners_data.name: Mollys Dolly
runners_data.note: Trainer David O'Brien has a 1/5 14-day record which is a mild positive; this horse sits naturally at the rear and being shown at midfield reflects field congestion rather than natural style — Good ground and 20f runs in best form.|
runners_data.comment: Held at Listowel last time back in a handicap, and her form has been patchy with two recent pull-ups in her record; best suited to a sound surface and shorter trips than today. Has been inconsistent, and there are questions over how reliable her earlier form was at this level.

runners_data.name: Tennesse Boy
runners_data.note: Returned a distant pull-up on comeback 245 days ago (previous run); showed a second over 26f on Good in historical form which suits the trip, but the fade-in-finish tag and redistribution from true hold-up position are both negatives.|
runners_data.comment: Last seen pulled up in a maiden at Ballingarry, and switching back to hurdling as a well-exposed maiden after pointing, he faces a stiff task; two pull-ups in his last five starts are a concern. Wears a first-time tongue-tie and handles 3m, but needs substantial improvement to figure.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who handles 26f on Good well with a win and multiple places; trainer Ryan's 2/29 14-day record catches the eye, and the tongue-tie points to a forward-going run — likely to feature prominently.|
runners_data.comment: Back over hurdles and well beaten at Sligo last time, not quite matching his form over fences; does arrive on a fair mark based on his chase performances, and handles today's trip and going. First-time tongue-tie fitted; yet to score over hurdles in recent starts but is versatile across conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Charlie's Dilemma is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, critically, faces no meaningful pressure from a genuine rival for the lead — this horse can dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over 2m6½f on Good ground. Illtakehimmyself, Le Fanu, U Asking Me and Smallcraftwarning will push forward to prominent positions, creating a small but competitive lead group, yet none of them is wired to seize the front and force Charlie's Dilemma off its rhythm. The result is a race likely run at an honest but unforced pace, with the front-runner able to conserve energy and potentially steal a winning break off the home turn. This shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace — patient hold-up types will find the tempo insufficient to set up a dramatic late surge, and with the field redistributed heavily toward the rear, the prominent profile is the one to be on.

watchPoints.text: Charlie's Dilemma has no challengers for the lead in a 19-runner field — watch whether it is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged, as that would dramatically increase its winning chance from the front.|
Le Fanu won last time over 20f on Good and will push forward promptly; if it travels easily behind Charlie's Dilemma in second or third, it becomes a serious danger to everything from two out.|
Sallap and Friends Of Barry both carry fade-in-finish flags at 2m6½f — if the pace is not strong enough to bring them into it turning for home, they are unlikely to sustain their effort to the line.|
Smallcraftwarning has a prominent style and a trainer in decent 14-day form; it has course-relevant stamina at 26f and could outrun its odds if it travels smoothly in the chasing group.|

The field contains seven redistributed true hold-up horses — Stone Rulya, Whatafoolbelieves, Liss Eile, Ballinaboola Gold, Can't Catch Molly, Mollys Dolly and Tennesse Boy — none of whom will naturally get to the rear; watch for traffic and interference issues in the pack from the start.|

races.name: Munster Suite At Limerick Races Handicap Hurdle (0-100)

runners_data.name: Mickey Hulie
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who should dictate throughout; recent course winner in form (1 from last 5), though his best ground figures come on Soft and his style fit of 0.92 reflects he may struggle if pressed earlier than expected by a large field.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here last time, hitting the line 2½l clear off a 7lb lower mark on softer ground; hitting his stride and effective at around 3m. Quicker conditions here could count against him, but he is the type to build on that confidence-booster.

runners_data.name: Ishan
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer with reasonable Good-ground credentials (5 places from 15 runs) but a string of mid-pack finishes recently including two PUs; the 2m6½f trip is the furthest he'll have gone and stamina is a query.|
runners_data.comment: Below his best in recent starts, his last outing saw him fare poorly in a shorter-trip handicap hurdle on quick ground; form suggests he is better suited over today's distance with some cut. Needs to bounce back sharply on a fair mark.

runners_data.name: Fire Coral
runners_data.note: Two recent wins at 2m and 2m4f on Good ground give this seven-year-old a strong profile for today's conditions; prominent style suits a sustainable gallop and the tongue tie is a consistent headgear flag — this is one of the more compelling profiles in the race.|
runners_data.comment: A pulled-up reappearance at Clonmel last time is best overlooked as a comeback run, with her prior record showing back-to-back wins; first-time tongue-tie applied. Effective at today's distance on a sound surface, and there is form from earlier in the season to build on.

runners_data.name: The Rebel County
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator wearing a hood; best form on Good (1 win, 2 places from 11 similar-going runs) and three successive top-four finishes including a third last time; needs a stronger pace than Mickey Hulie is likely to set to get involved from the back.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Downpatrick last time when beaten 4l off a 13lb higher mark, suggesting he holds a fair position in this sphere; cheekpieces fitted for the first time. Effective over today's trip and going, though the evidence points to him being a shade better over fences.

runners_data.name: Technology
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 269 days off for Alan King; showed promise at 2m4f on Good before his break but a nine-month layoff is a significant concern in a competitive 19-runner handicap at this distance.|
runners_data.comment: Returning from a nine-month absence, he had no answer to the gallop in a strongly run race at Tipperary most recently, failing to see out the distance; first-time hood and tongue-tie applied. A frustrating maiden, but effective over today's range.

runners_data.name: Ellies Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent style but recent runs show inconsistency including a fall last time; best form at 2m or shorter on Good, and the step up to 2m6½f may stretch stamina for an eight-year-old who hasn't won at this trip.|
runners_data.comment: A chase fall here last time, and she has been inconsistent across recent outings with a mixed record; the switch back to hurdling may suit better, and she has shown she can win in this sphere. Acts with cut but our figures place her well down the order.

runners_data.name: Gortmore Lady
runners_data.note: One of the more authentic hold-up types in the field; has placed four times in her last five Good-ground runs without winning and Darragh O'Keeffe is a significant jockey booking — the 2m6½f trip and Good ground both suit, though a slow pace is her biggest danger.|
runners_data.comment: Brought down last time and pulled up the start before — her form figures look worse than they are, with interference accounting for the latest exit; effective over today's trip and acts on good ground. A frustrating maiden, though the trainer's recent record is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Whatyouwant
runners_data.note: 279 days off the track is a major concern for this eight-year-old despite having won at 2m5f on Good; hood noted and he is a prominent racer at his best, but the extended absence outweighs the style suitability.|
runners_data.comment: Below par on a Flat outing at The Curragh most recently, but she has shown ability over hurdles including a win; cheekpieces applied for the first time. Prone to inconsistency and likely to need this comeback run after a lengthy absence, but effective at around 3m on good ground.

runners_data.name: Knocknagoran Lady
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who placed at 2m4f on Good last time; the step up to 2m6½f could suit given pedigree, though the tongue tie and visor combination suggests she has idiosyncrasies that can limit her finishing effort.|
runners_data.comment: Front-running tactics at Wexford last time backfired as she was left well held; tongue-tie and visor fitted for the first time. Effective over this distance range on good and heavy ground, but needs to show more restraint to build on recent efforts.

runners_data.name: Ballyredinkingston
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has struggled for form recently (three unplaced runs including a brought-down); 17 days since last run is quick for a six-year-old with this level of form, and no wins on Good going in five attempts.|
runners_data.comment: Sixth at Kilbeggan last time on his first start over an extended trip, which was a fair enough effort at the level; acts on today's conditions and holds a reasonable position at the weights. Needs to build further, but the step up in distance appears to suit and he merits respect.

runners_data.name: Western Opera
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer whose best effort was a second at 2m2f on Good; the 2m6½f trip is significantly further than anything he has shown stamina for, and the tongue tie flags a tendency to pull — a difficult assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Finished with running to spare over a below-par trip at Clonmel last time, beaten 4l but seemingly crying out for more emphasis on stamina; top-rated in our assessments and effective over today's distance and going. Tongue-tie fitted for the first time; inconsistency is the only caveat.

runners_data.name: Hob's Angel
runners_data.note: Two recent wins including a course-distance win last time at 2m on Good; the prominent style fits perfectly with Mickey Hulie's likely pace, and despite being a ten-year-old, the sharp uptick in form (1-2 in last two) makes this a live contender.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a win at Clonmel two starts ago, then ran to her mark when runner-up here last time; off the same official rating now and showing consistency over this distance and ground. Capable of getting into the places off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Phildante
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a consistent mid-pack finishing pattern and no wins in recent Good-ground starts; the 2m6½f distance is on the long side for his best form and the presence of so many hold-up rivals means he will need an exceptional run through.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth and beaten 9l at Sligo most recently, running to modest form in a pattern that has seen her well held across recent starts; tongue-tie and cheekpieces worn for the first time. An unreliable maiden who has yet to show enough to suggest she can make a significant impact here.

runners_data.name: Lady Aquarelle
runners_data.note: True hold-up type flagged as fading in the finish; mapped to midfield because of excess hold-up runners in this field — her natural position will be near the rear, which compounds the fade concern over this demanding trip.|
runners_data.comment: Well held despite having a clear passage here last time, and the form figures make grim reading across recent starts; cheekpieces fitted for the first time. Rated off a basement mark but needs to find more, and today's extended trip looks likely to stretch her further.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose recent form includes multiple pulled-up efforts; though mapped midfield by redistribution, he will likely drift to the back of the pack naturally and the tongue tie plus a poor recent record makes this a difficult proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Three of her last five starts have ended in a pull-up, form that has deteriorated markedly in recent outings; tongue-tie applied for the first time. Most effective at shorter distances, so today's extended trip poses a significant additional question.

runners_data.name: Annie Questions
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up runner flagged as fading in the finish; her redistribution to midfield overstates her likely position, and an eight-year-old with no wins from nine Good-ground runs in recent form is not ideally placed for this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Roscommon on her latest start under rules; a winner in point-to-point form who has yet to reproduce that on the track, and the first-time hood is an aid designed to sharpen her focus. Something to find, but distance and going are familiar.

runners_data.name: Captain Kate
runners_data.note: Returning from 231 days off, this hold-up mare has never won on Good going and has a string of sixth-place finishes at longer trips; pushed into midfield on the map but will likely track back to her natural rear position.|
runners_data.comment: Off the track for over seven months since a pull-up at Punchestown where she never settled and the ground was against her; cheekpieces fitted for the first time. Most effective on a sound surface over this trip, but her maiden profile looks well exposed at this level.

runners_data.name: Tuff Days
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer who cannot secure his natural position in this 19-runner field; nine-year-old without a win in 15 Good-ground starts, and with the style fit compromised, he is hard to recommend in this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: In poor form at Kilbeggan last time, well beaten in a handicap hurdle; an exposed maiden who has found little in recent outings despite familiar distance and going. Hard to make a strong case for him at current figures.

runners_data.name: Another Glendaars
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer without a jockey listed — a significant concern at declaration stage; consistent mid-pack finisher at shorter trips (best form at 2m-2m2f) and the 2m6½f looks beyond his proven stamina range.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Downpatrick latest, held up and left with too much ground to make up in the closing stages; capable of better when getting a cleaner passage through the race. Our figures place him in the leading group and he acts on today's conditions, though he must confirm that promise under a searching test.

races.paceDynamic: Mickey Hulie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 19-runner field and, with no genuine challenger likely to press him hard from the outset, he should control tempo over 2m6½f on Good ground at Limerick — a trip that rewards those who can conserve energy through the middle stages. The pace is likely to be honest but not brutal, with Mickey Hulie able to dictate his own rhythm, which historically suits prominent horses that travel close to the leader and pounce before the final hurdle rather than deep closers who need a stronger gallop to reel rivals in. Several hold-up operators — Lady Aquarelle, Set The Tone, Annie Questions, Captain Kate — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains far more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; in reality they will likely find themselves further back than ideal, with Set The Tone, Lady Aquarelle and Annie Questions the ones most likely to be squeezed into their natural rearward berth. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can travel close to Mickey Hulie's sustainable gallop and quicken at the business end of this Grade-3 trip are the profiles to favour, with pure hold-up horses facing a tough ask if the pace never truly ignites.

watchPoints.text: Fire Coral has won twice at similar trips on Good going recently and is the most profile-matched prominent horse behind Mickey Hulie — watch whether Phillip Enright allows her to slot directly behind the leader from the outset.|

Mickey Hulie's ability to control the pace unchallenged is the hinge of this entire race — if a prominent rival like Ishan or Ellies Rock pushes him harder than expected from the early stages, the tempo could unravel and compress the finish.|

Gortmore Lady with Darragh O'Keeffe is the most dangerous hold-up horse in the field — if the pace quickens enough from three out, watch where she sits at the top of the home straight, as four places from five recent Good-ground runs suggests she finds the line.|

Hob's Angel arrives on the back of a career-best sequence (two from two recently including a 2m win on Good) and at OR=78 carries a relatively light weight — his prominent style makes him naturally well-placed if Mickey Hulie sets a sustainable gallop.|

Another Glendaars is flagged without a confirmed jockey — monitor markets and declarations closely, as a late rider booking or withdrawal would shift the field dynamics slightly in a race where every prominent-position horse matters at 19 runners.|

races.name: INPBA Supporting Irish Racing Flat Race (In Memory Of Jerry McDonnell)

runners_data.name: Bacharach
runners_data.comment: Second at Ballinrobe last time on just his second career start, though he may have gone to the front a little sooner than ideal; should remain competitive as he develops further. Effective at today's trip on good ground, wearing a tongue-tie today, and has the profile of a horse with more to come.

runners_data.name: Caislean Gear
runners_data.comment: Pulled clear of the remainder on his sole outing at Roscommon, finishing second behind a more experienced rival; top-rated here and looks the type to build on that promising introduction. His connections have a strong record in this sphere, and he handles today's trip well.

runners_data.name: Frisco Lad
runners_data.comment: A debut runner by Walk In The Park, from a dam placed in points; the market will be the best guide to his chance on first appearance. In the hands of a top trainer, though a half-brother to a poor performer at an extended trip means ability cannot be assumed.

runners_data.name: Mountain Sky
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on his sole start at Killarney, and as a flat-bred returning from a short break, he faces a significant gap to close against more experienced rivals; tongue-tie applied for the first time today. Lightly raced, but needs to show considerably more to be a factor here.

runners_data.name: River Cartwright
runners_data.comment: An unraced Kew Gardens gelding making his debut; a half-brother to a useful performer at an extended trip, and his stable has a history of landing debutants in this sphere. Ranked lowest on our figures, but the starting price will be the clearest guide to his chance.

runners_data.name: Time For Talking
runners_data.comment: Third on his debut at Ballinrobe despite his jockey losing an iron early in the race; a promising introduction against more seasoned rivals, and he should take a step forward with that experience behind him. Effective at today's trip and going, and rates as a live danger to the top two.

runners_data.name: Village Star
runners_data.comment: Unraced on his debut, his breeding offers limited encouragement for this sphere; a full-brother to a moderate performer at 17 furlongs, with his dam's best form over sprint distances on the Flat. Probably one to monitor rather than actively support on first appearance.

runners_data.name: Maggies Yard
runners_data.comment: An unraced Pillar Coral filly making her debut here; a half-sister to a moderate performer at an extended trip, though another relative has been successful in points and over hurdles. Faces a stiff ask against more experienced rivals on first appearance.

runners_data.name: The President
runners_data.comment: Third on debut at Listowel, beaten 20 lengths in a mares bumper, though the form has since taken some knocks; represents a top yard and looks capable of showing considerably more with further experience. Handles today's trip and going, and rates as one of the leading threats to the selection.
